ana: Starting canary bring-up for notch22b-int4 on g5-16x. Quant pass vs baseline but hitting occasional OOMs under mixed long requests. p99 spikes too.

jules: Can you paste allocator tail and request shapes?

ana: tail: ```[2026-03-21T12:02:10Z] kv_reserve: requested 1.4GB -> fail
[2026-03-21T12:02:10Z] evict: freed 200MB
[2026-03-21T12:02:11Z] oom: worker killed pid 2245``` mostly prompts with gen ~300-600 tokens.

farah: Likely combo of large max_new_tokens + aggressive prefetch. For int4 22B we should be conservative. Proposal: set max_new_tokens=240, prefetch_window=24, batch_limit=4, kv_slot_reserve_ratio=0.08 for canary.

jules: Also add soft-router rewrite: if incoming max_new_tokens > 400 rewrite to 240 and annotate request.reason="safety:max_new_tokens". And add fallback to notch13b-lite on allocation failure.

ana: Rolling canary with those settings to 2 hosts now.

infra-bot: Alert rule created: eng-ml.notch22b.oom_rate > 0.005 over 15m -> notify #eng-oncall.

ana: Running quick synthetic driver (mix short/long) and will post p95/p99 + OOMs.

ana: Results after change: 150 jobs, OOMs=0, p95 down 730ms->420ms, p99 down 1.8s->1.25s, kv_eviction_rate up slightly. Keeping canary config and drafting catalog note recommending conservative defaults for quantized 20B+ models.

farah: Good. Follow-up: instrument continuous-batcher to track inflight_tokens and add soft-throttle if inflight_tokens>12k. Open PR for catalog and runbook.

jules: Thanks, all :thumbsup:
